title: Remittance Acceptance and Funds Timing Schedule — Payoff and Loan Satisfaction
content:
Remittance and funds settings for the Payoff and Loan Satisfaction product. They state how payoff funds may be sent, how long late or short funds are tolerated or held, and when funds are applied, refunded or returned.

| Setting | Borrower Voluntary Payoff | HECM-to-HECM Refinance Payoff | Heir Retention Payoff | Estate Market Sale Payoff | Approved Short Sale Payoff | Deed in Lieu of Foreclosure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ways payoff funds may be remitted | wire; cashier's check | wire | wire; cashier's check | wire | wire | none (no funds are taken) |
| A personal check is accepted as payoff funds | no | no | no | no | no | no |
| Calendar days after the good-through date within which funds are still accepted with additional daily accrual | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| Calendar days insufficient funds are held on the case before they are returned to the remitter | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Business days after satisfaction within which funds above the required payoff are refunded to the remitter | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| Calendar days after satisfaction within which the lien release is sent for recording | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Refinance payoff funds are accepted only after the new loan's rescission period ended | no | yes | no | no | no | no |
| When held funds are applied to the loan | on the satisfaction date | on the satisfaction date | on the satisfaction date | on the satisfaction date | on the satisfaction date | on the satisfaction date |
| Who receives a refund of excess or returned funds | the original remitter | the original remitter | the original remitter | the original remitter | the original remitter | the original remitter |
| What happens when remitted funds are recalled or dishonored | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens | the receipt is reversed and the shortfall reopens |

### Points of judgement

1. A cashier's check is accepted only on the Borrower Voluntary Payoff and the Heir Retention Payoff; the other funds-based plans take wires only, and the Deed in Lieu of Foreclosure takes no funds.
2. No plan accepts a personal check.
3. The 5-day tolerance after the good-through date, the 30-day holding period for short funds, the 10-business-day refund period and the 30-day lien-release period are the same on every plan.
4. The rescission-period condition applies to the HECM-to-HECM Refinance Payoff alone.

### Hypothetical tolerance illustration

For a hypothetical statement good through the 10th day of a month, the 5 tolerance days are the 11th through the 15th; funds received on the 15th fall inside the tolerance and funds received on the 16th fall outside it. The dates are illustrative only.
